rules.T1: The file is a Google Trends "Interest over time" download for Ghana: a Week column, then one column per term marked (Ghana).
rules.T2: Weeks follow each other exactly seven days apart, with none missing.
rules.T3: Every value is a whole number from 0 to 100, or "<1".
rules.T4: Some term reaches 100 in some week: Google scales each download to its busiest week.
rules.T5: It covers about five years (at least 250 weeks).

source: Google Trends (https://trends.google.com), web search, Ghana, past 5 years

text.lede: What people in Ghana search for on Google, week by week over five years: 20 terms in 4 groups. It shows what people are paying attention to, not what they think of it, and only among people who search online.
text.cedi-h2: Ghanaians search for the cedi when it moves fast
text.cedi-p: The four busiest months for ‘cedi’ searches were May 2025, December 2022, June 2025 and October 2022. All four are among the six months when the cedi moved most against the dollar: the dollar's price in cedis rose 27.7% in October 2022, fell 23.2% in December 2022 and fell 20.7% in May 2025. Month by month, searches and the size of the cedi's move go together (correlation 0.68 over 56 months, Bank of Ghana monthly averages). Searches show the moves get noticed; they can't say why the cedi moved.
text.prices-h2: ‘fuel price’ draws the most searches about prices
text.prices-p: ‘fuel price’ is searched 3.8 times as often as ‘petrol price’, the next term in the group, and peaked in the week of 26 Apr 2026. ‘petrol price’, ‘food prices’, ‘price of rice’ and ‘transport fare’ are searched too little to read week to week; their monthly averages are on the chart. Below it, all-items inflation over the same months, from TARIN's CPI.
text.power-h2: Searches about power cuts have jumped
text.power-p: ‘power outage’ searches over the last four weeks were 4.2 times their level in the year before. ‘ECG’ (the Electricity Company of Ghana), the group's most searched term, peaked in the week of 26 Apr 2026. In the IEA's May 2026 survey, electricity supply was the second most common reason people gave for disapproving of the president's performance (29.9%), after the economy: see the opinion polls.
text.jobs-p: ‘jobs’ is the most searched term in the group. ‘recruitment’ and ‘WASSCE results’ come in sharp bursts: their busiest weeks (16 Nov 2025 and 30 Aug 2026) were 6 and 15.5 times their five-year averages.

text.tile-1-l: the week of 26 Apr 2026 was the busiest for ‘fuel price’ searches
text.tile-2-l: ‘power outage’ searches, last four weeks against the year before
text.tile-3-l: ‘WASSCE results’ searches in the week of 30 Aug 2026, against their five-year average
text.m-data: The data. Google Trends' “interest over time” for web searches in Ghana, weekly, for the past five years, in 4 downloads of five terms each. 100 is the busiest week for any term in its download, so terms compare within a group but not across groups. A value Google shows as “<1” is counted as 0.5. Google changed how it collects the data on 1 January 2022, so early-2022 steps may be partly that change.
text.m-how: How it's collected. Google Trends has no open API (its official one is an invite-only trial) and treats automated use of its website as scraping, so the files are downloaded by hand from trends.google.com about once a month. TARIN files each one byte for byte with its SHA-256 fingerprint and checks it before it is used. Each new download rescales the whole five years, so it replaces the last one; the old files stay archived.
